detailed_analysis: This is an AFM height map of mica in 10 mM KCl, imaged at ~0.043 nm/px (after resampling anisotropic 0.043/0.086 nm/px pixels to square). The overarching goal is to characterize surface structure/adsorbate patterning. The extracted features fall into two very different confidence tiers. TRUSTWORTHY (lateral, scale-derived): the in-plane XY scale is verified from metadata (scale_uncertain=False), so length scales are physically meaningful. The autocorrelation correlation length is 0.87 nm and the mid-frequency radial-PSD corrugation wavelength is 0.82 nm (ratio 1.07) — these two independent estimators agree closely, indicating a real, laterally short-ranged surface texture with a characteristic repeat/decorrelation scale just under 1 nm. Coverage of ~0.55 with mean patch size ~0.59 nm and 109 patches describes a finely divided, roughly half-and-half two-level surface — consistent with a patchy, sub-nm-scale adsorbate/hydration-layer coverage or ion-condensation domains on mica, NOT a well-ordered crystalline lattice. A low-frequency PSD envelope at L~11 nm captures the larger-scale mottling/height undulation visible in the leveled image. UNTRUSTWORTHY / ARTIFACTUAL: (1) The z-calibration FAILED. The metadata data range is only ~6 pm (−309.5 to −315.5 pm) yet Rq is reported as ~5936 in raw uint16 counts (z_calibrated=False). This is an uncalibrated dtype value, not a height — the true Rq should be sub-nm (order a few pm). Rq is correctly EXCLUDED from cross-concentration comparison and should not be interpreted as roughness. All PSD amplitudes (mid_freq_peak_amplitude ~1.1e13) inherit this failure and are in arbitrary counts^2, so no amplitude-derived quantity is physical. (2) The 'reflection' at d=0.490 nm (sigma=3.2, 15 reflections) is almost certainly an ARTIFACT. The FFT panel shows only a strong vertical streak (residual scan-line/row correlation), not discrete Bragg spots, and the reflection amplitude map is a smooth low-frequency blob rather than a localized reciprocal-lattice spot. Although 0.49 nm is tantalizingly near mica's ~0.52 nm lattice spacing, both raw and leveled images look amorphous/featureless by eye, and the corrugation/correlation scale (~0.82-0.87 nm) does not match 0.49 nm. The 0.49 nm signal most plausibly encodes the streak/noise periodicity, not the mica lattice. (3) Overall vision verification scored 0.43 (below 0.7) using a reused locked script — the image may not match the intended series, so ALL features are low-confidence. In summary: the data support a sub-nm-scale, patchy, disordered surface texture, but do NOT support a resolved crystalline mica lattice, and yield no calibrated height/roughness information.

scientific_claims.claim: The mica-in-KCl surface exhibits a laterally short-ranged, sub-nanometer texture with a characteristic scale of ~0.85 nm, corroborated by two independent estimators (autocorrelation correlation length 0.87 nm and mid-frequency PSD corrugation wavelength 0.82 nm; ratio 1.07), consistent with a patchy adsorbate/hydration structure (coverage ~0.55, mean patch ~0.59 nm) rather than a resolved periodic lattice.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: A sub-nm decorrelation length with ~50% two-level coverage points to nanoscale ion/hydration patterning at the mica-electrolyte interface, relevant to understanding ion adsorption, Stern-layer structure, and hydration-layer organization on charged mineral surfaces.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed a sub-nanometer (~0.85 nm) correlation length with roughly half-monolayer patchy coverage on mica in dilute KCl by AFM?

analysis_approach: Preprocess (row-level + square-pixel resample + z-calibrate), then use targeted reciprocal-space reflection mapping to test quantitatively whether any resolvable periodic lattice survives at 10 mM, and characterize the surface texture via radial PSD length scales and physical roughness.

issues.problem: Rq is reported as 5935.78 in raw z-units with Rq_z_calibrated=false and Rq_units='z-units'. The plan required Rq in pm, physically plausible for near-atomically-flat mica (sub-nm, on the order of the ~6 pm z-range). A dimensionless/dtype value orders of magnitude off (~5900 vs expected ~few pm) is exactly the broken-unit-mapping bug the domain criteria say to flag.

A 'periodic reflection' at 0.49 nm is reported as detected (n_reflections_detected=15, null_flag=false), but the raw and leveled images show only isotropic granular texture with no lattice, and the FFT power panel shows only a vertical streak (slow-scan/1D scan artifact) with no discrete Bragg spots. The 'reflection amplitude' map is a smooth low-frequency blob field, not a localized discrete-spot domain. This is almost certainly noise/scan-texture passing a marginal 3.2-sigma floor, not a real mica lattice (mica's ~0.52 nm surface lattice would appear as symmetric hexagonal spots, not a diffuse blob).

The 109-patch domain segmentation with coverage 0.55 is a threshold of a diffuse amplitude/texture field, not a physically meaningful domain census. Given the reflection itself is dubious, these 'patches' likely trace noise contours.

The vertical streak in the FFT (and residual horizontal banding still visible in the leveled topography) indicates row-median leveling did not fully suppress scan-line structure; streak_fraction=0.04 is low but the dominant FFT feature is still the scan-direction streak.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Fix the z-to-pm calibration and report Rq in pm; then tighten the reflection significance gate (min_sigma 4-5 + require discrete spot_snr_domain >> bulk) so the analysis either confirms a real lattice or reports the legitimate 'no resolvable lattice at 10 mM' null.
